input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects that the accessibility
audit enumerated across the four core Dashboard flows — project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each
flow is fully operable with keyboard alone and focus indicators are visibly
consistent.

## Scope

- Fix each defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited flows:
  - focus lost in modals (focus not moved into the dialog on open, not
    restored to the invoking control on close, or trapped inside the dialog)
  - controls unreachable via keyboard (tab order, missing focusability,
    pointer-only interactions)
  - inconsistent or invisible focus indicators on interactive controls
- Apply a consistent visible focus-indicator treatment across the interactive
  controls of the audited flows
- Verify each of the four flows end-to-end with keyboard only, against the
  audit's per-flow defect list
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require, and flows outside the four audited ones

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using
  keyboard only, and every defect enumerated in the audit report for that
  flow is verified fixed
- No focus traps remain: focus moves into modals when they open, returns to
  the invoking control when they close, and is never lost mid-flow
- Every interactive control in the audited flows is reachable and operable
  via keyboard
- Focus indicators are visibly consistent across all interactive controls in
  the audited flows
- A recorded keyboard-only walkthrough of each of the four flows documents
  the verification

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: the four audited core flows fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: visible focus indicators consistent across the audited
  flows — same remediation pass over the same flows and surfaces as HLR-1;
  bundled here because a split would re-audit the same controls twice

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates the accessibility conformance documentation — the VPAT and
the product documentation accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed
state of the four core Dashboard flows, and republishes both through the
standard documentation process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- VPAT: revise the conformance levels for the success criteria affected by
  the keyboard-accessibility remediation of the four audited flows (project
  creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission),
  reflecting the post-fix state
- Product documentation accessibility statement: update to describe the
  remediated keyboard operability and focus-indicator state of the audited
  flows
- Republish the updated VPAT and accessibility statement through the
  standard docs publishing process

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT's per-criterion conformance levels for the four audited flows
  reflect the implemented post-fix behavior
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented fixes —
  engineering confirms the documented conformance matches the shipped
  behavior of the four flows
- The republished documents are publicly available at their documented
  locations

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

## Triage

Not below-threshold and not docs-only: the strategy spans an active code
component (Dashboard) and a substantive content-authoring work stream
(VPAT and accessibility-statement republication on the Documentation
component). Code implementation plus substantive documentation authoring
are distinct work streams (different skills, review criteria, and PR
cycles), so the strategy is decomposed into a two-epic DAG.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Component | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P1 |
| E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHAI Documentation | Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001: Keyboard a11y remediation (Dashboard, P1)"] --> E002["E002: VPAT + accessibility statement update (Documentation, P2)"]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The VPAT and accessibility statement describe the fixed state of the four flows; they cannot be written or republished accurately until the keyboard remediation lands. Per the docs-authoring priority exception this edge does not trigger priority inheritance — E002 stays P2. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|-----|----------|------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows — the audit enumerates exact defects per flow |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E001 | Focus-indicator consistency is part of the same remediation pass over the same flows and surfaces as HLR-1; not separately schedulable, kept bundled in one epic |
| HLR-3 | P2 | E002 | docs-authoring epic; priority also derives from strategy `priority: Normal` → P2 per the docs-authoring priority exception |

## Component Mapping

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Team | Classification |
|--------------------|---------------------|------|----------------|
| Dashboard | Dashboard | RHOAI Dashboard | Active — code changes (per architecture context `architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`) |
| Documentation | Documentation | RHAI Documentation (assumed) | Content authoring (VPAT + accessibility statement) |

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Epic ACs were derived from the HLRs and the
  problem statement. In particular, the owner team for the Documentation work
  is not stated anywhere in the strategy or in architecture context (no
  context file exists for Documentation); it was assigned to "RHAI
  Documentation" by assumption and should be confirmed before scheduling.
- **Schedule pressure on the critical path**: two public-sector customers
  require the republished VPAT before renewal. Both epics sit on the critical
  path (E001 → E002), so slippage in the remediation directly delays the
  conformance statement. This is a schedule constraint, not an AC.
- **Priority note**: HLR-3 is P2 but is renewal-blocking for two customers per
  the problem statement; the strategy's P2 label may understate its urgency.
  Flagged for human verification; priorities kept as stated.

### 7. Completeness (2/2)

score.feedback:
decomposition_quality 5/5 — SCORE: 5

**The probed failure was avoided.** This is the inverse triage probe: the annotation warns that the strategy looks small enough to collapse into a single below-threshold epic or a code+docs bundle. The decomposition did neither — `triage: null`, two epics, with HLR-3 split into its own docs-authoring epic. This is exactly the expected shape (2–3 epics, no triage, docs epic sequenced after the code fixes it describes, with a technical-review AC).

**1. HLR coverage — solid.** All three HLRs mapped: HLR-1 and HLR-2 to E001, HLR-3 to E002, each epic carrying an HLR Traceability section and the summary a full matrix. Bundling HLR-1+HLR-2 into E001 is the right call — they are the same remediation pass over the same four flows and surfaces, and splitting them would put two epics on the same UI surface — and the bundling is recorded with inline justification rather than silently absorbed. Priority inheritance is correct: E001 is P1 blocking no P0 work; E002 stays P2 under the docs-authoring exemption, and the DAG justification explicitly records that the edge does not trigger inheritance.

**2. Epic boundaries — solid.** Clean component/team split (Dashboard/RHOAI Dashboard vs Documentation/RHAI Documentation), code remediation strictly separated from content authoring — the work-product split the probe demands. E001 is a defect-list-driven pass, plausibly ~2 weeks; E002 is a bounded docs update. No surface duplication. The assumed "RHAI Documentation" owner is flagged in Health Warnings for confirmation rather than silently asserted.

**3. DAG quality — solid.** Single edge E001 → E002 matches E002's frontmatter dependency and E001's empty dependency list; the Mermaid arrow runs dependency → dependent. The edge is the rule-mandated docs-authoring-last edge with a sound rationale (the conformance statement describes the fixed state). Nothing parallel-eligible is serialized — with one implementation epic and one docs epic that genuinely consumes its output, a length-2 critical path is the correct shape.

**4. Scope fidelity — solid.** No invented API paths, CRD fields, env vars, or response formats. E001's unpacking of "focus lost in modals" into open/restore/trap modes is standard a11y defect taxonomy for verification, not design; the focus-indicator AC deliberately does not prescribe a treatment. E002 stays at "reflect post-fix conformance levels" without inventing criterion numbers or levels. Neither epic body references sibling draft IDs.

**5. Acceptance criteria — solid.** E001's ACs are testable per-flow against the audit's enumerated defects, with a recorded walkthrough as evidence. E002 carries the rule-mandated docs-authoring technical-review AC ("engineering confirms the documented conformance matches the shipped behavior"). No rollback/feature-flag or build-pipeline ACs are needed (no replacement work, no konflux chain). The "publicly available at documented locations" AC conditions the epic's own deliverable, and the renewal schedule pressure is correctly placed in Health Warnings as risk, not as an AC.

Minor observations that don't rise to gaps: "visibly consistent" indicators is mildly soft, but it is HLR-2's own language and is made testable by the applied-treatment AC plus the walkthrough; the strategy's missing teams/NFR/GWT sections and the P2-understatement of renewal-blocking HLR-3 are all surfaced in Health Warnings rather than dropped. The decomposition is a clean, correct handling of a trap case. | [informational] internal adversarial review score 14/14
